_comment: Default fallback note for Claire — represents a real human care manager (Lisa Goldenstein, SurveyHealth) follow-up call. Loaded by default and when ?mock=1 is present. Overridden by live Quo + LLM output when 'Listen for AI call' captures a fresh call.

callMeta.agentName: Lisa Goldenstein, RN — SurveyHealth Care Manager

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hi Claire, this is Lisa from SurveyHealth calling on behalf of Everyday Health Clinic. Is now still a good time to talk for a couple of minutes?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, yes, it is. Thanks for calling back so quickly.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Of course. I'm following up on the check-in you did earlier this week. You mentioned more shortness of breath and a cough that's been bothering you — is that still going on today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: It is. I've been coughing up a lot more, and honestly it doesn't look good. Even getting up the stairs is hard now.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Okay, thank you for telling me. And how about your medications — are you confident you're taking the right doses?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Not really. I'm a little confused on which one is which. My daughter usually helps but she's been away.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: That's helpful for me to know. Have you felt at any point this week that you needed to be seen — even if you didn't end up calling anyone?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes. There was one night I almost called, but I didn't want to be a hassle. Maybe I should have.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're not a hassle, Claire. That's exactly what we're here for. Compared to last month, would you say you're feeling better, worse, or about the same?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Worse. Definitely worse. I'm not getting better, and I think I need to be seen.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Okay. Any new pain, fever, nausea, vomiting — anything else that's new this past month?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, none of that. It's mainly the breathing and the cough.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Got it. Here's what I'd like to do. I'm going to get you on the schedule today or tomorrow with Dr. Henderson's team — I think you should be seen sooner rather than later. In the meantime, please continue your furosemide in the morning and the lisinopril as prescribed.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: And one more thing — I'm going to send you a quick text so you can take your blood pressure and weight on your phone. It only takes about a minute and helps the team see what's happening before your visit.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Perfect. If anything gets worse before we talk again — chest pain, severe shortness of breath at rest, or you feel lightheaded — please call 911 right away. I'll be in touch within the next two hours with your appointment time. Take care, Claire.

note.goals: No ED visits and no hospitalizations this calendar year.
note.evaluationReason: Follow-up to flagged biweekly wellness check — patient reported worsening dyspnea, increased cough, medication confusion, and a self-identified need for clinical attention.
note.summaryOfInteraction: Spoke with Ms. Henderson by phone for 2 minutes and 47 seconds. Patient reports progressive shortness of breath when climbing stairs over the past 7–9 days, an increase in cough volume and productivity, mild bilateral ankle swelling in the evenings, and a 3-lb weight gain from last week. New orthopnea — needing to prop up on pillows overnight. Denies chest pain, palpitations, fever, nausea, or vomiting. Medication adherence uncertain — patient confused about which doses she's taking; usual support from daughter is currently unavailable. Patient expressed she felt she should have been seen earlier in the week. Compared to last month, patient reports her general wellness is worse and explicitly stated she needs to be seen.
note.plan:
1. Schedule same-day or next-day visit with Dr. Henderson's team; nurse to confirm appointment within 2 hours.
2. Reconcile medications on next call — confirm furosemide AM dose and lisinopril; offer pill-organizer setup with daughter when she returns.
3. Send RPM prompt for BP and weight reading; alert threshold +2 lb/day or +5 lb/week.
4. Reinforce 2 g sodium diet and fluid guidance; reviewed CHF decompensation warning signs with patient.
5. Patient instructed to call 911 if chest pain, severe SOB at rest, or lightheadedness develops before her visit.
6. Flag ticket as Evaluation — High priority pending PCP review.

summary.oneLine: Likely early CHF decompensation — worsening dyspnea, productive cough, new orthopnea, 3-lb weight gain, and medication confusion. Same-day clinic visit being arranged.
